newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians, Ukrainian set for 1997 shuttle flights.
newsitem.headline: Russians, Ukrainian set for 1997 shuttle flights.

text.p: Two Russians and a Ukrainian are to make separate 10-day trips to the Russian orbiting space station Mir next year aboard U.S. space shuttle craft, Itar-Tass news agency said on Friday.
It quoted the Russian Space Agency as saying veteran Russian cosmonauts Yelena Kondakova and Vladimir Titov would go in March and September respectively.
The Ukrainian shuttle member had still to be chosen from a list of five candidates. Tass said the decision would be made in January and the mission would take place in October.
Kondakova, who was part of the Mir crew when it made its first link up with the shuttle in June 1995, was already training in the United States, the agency added.

Kondakova held the record for a woman staying in space before U.S. astronaut Shannon Lucid broke it with a 188-day mission on Mir. That feat was partly helped by delays to relief missions, which continue to dog the 10-year-old space station.

The current Russian-American crew is stuck in space with toilets close to overflowing because the system which recycles their bodily waste fluids has broken down and they cannot find the pump that would let them transfer it to the cooling system.

A cargo vessel had been due to take off in October with new waste containers and supplies but the launch has been postponed to November 20 because cash problems have delayed the construction of the Soyuz rocket boosters needed for such craft.

The Mir crew also learned on Thursday that the launch of their replacement team, two Russians and a German, had been put back to February from December 15, also due to delays with the production of the Soyuz rockets.
